title: Democracy, Autocracy, or Something Else?
gist: Against both the liberal-convergence and authoritarian-wave narratives, the authors argue 21st-century political outcomes will be decided by mundane work on democratic accountability and institutional effectiveness — citing Hungary's April election, in which Péter Magyar's Tisza party ended Viktor Orbán's 16-year 'illiberal democracy' project.

insights.claim: The world is neither converging on liberal democracy nor being swept by an authoritarian tide — both dominant narratives about global political direction are wrong.
insights.speaker: HELMUT K. ANHEIER
insights.so_what: Argues against pricing a single global political regime trend; country-level institutional quality, not a global tide, drives political risk premia.
insights.quote: the world is neither converging on liberal democracy nor being swept by an authoritarian tide

insights.claim: The decisive political struggles of the 21st century will be won or lost through unglamorous work on democratic accountability and building effective institutions, not through dramatic regime-level shifts.
insights.speaker: HELMUT K. ANHEIER
insights.so_what: Points analysts toward measurable institutional-capacity indicators rather than regime labels when assessing sovereign and political risk.
insights.quote: The decisive political struggles of the 21st century will be won or lost through the unglamorous work of strengthening democratic accountability and building effective institutions.

insights.claim: In April, Hungarian voters ended Viktor Orbán's 16-year project of building an 'illiberal democracy,' handing Péter Magyar's Tisza party a landslide and making him prime minister.
insights.speaker: HELMUT K. ANHEIER
insights.so_what: A concrete regime reversal inside the EU — relevant to Hungarian assets, EU cohesion-funds disputes, and the bloc's unanimity votes on Russia policy.
insights.quote: Hungarians handed Péter Magyar’s Tisza party a landslide victory, making him prime minister
insights.locator: BERLIN—This year has been marked by striking political upheavals

insights.claim: The Hungarian opposition won despite Fidesz's manipulation of both public and private media, showing entrenched media capture is not by itself decisive at the ballot box.
insights.speaker: HELMUT K. ANHEIER
insights.so_what: Weakens the assumption that incumbent media control makes autocratic consolidation irreversible — raises implied volatility around entrenched-incumbent elections elsewhere.
insights.quote: Defying the odds and the Fidesz party’s manipulation of public and private media
insights.locator: Defying the odds and the Fidesz party
